parts.t: Buying your first home in BC? This free calculator shows your property transfer tax (PTT) with and without the first-time buyer exemption, whether a new home could get the GST rebate, and how an FHSA can help with your down payment. No sign-up needed.

blocks.text: How the first-time buyer PTT exemption works

parts.t: No PTT on the first $500,000 of the price if the home is worth $835,000 or less.
A partial exemption between $835,000 and $860,000.
You must move in within 92 days and live there as your main home for the first year.
Source:
Government of BC, First time home buyers' program
$480,000 condo: regular PTT $7,600. First-time buyer pays $0.
$650,000 townhome: regular PTT $11,000. First-time buyer pays $3,000.
$900,000 home: over $860,000, so no exemption. PTT $16,000.

blocks.text: New homes and the GST rebate

parts.t: First-time buyers of a new home can get back all of the 5% GST on homes up to $1 million, with a smaller rebate up to $1.5 million.

blocks.text: First-Time Buyer Calculator BC — Frequently Asked Questions

parts.t: What is the BC First-Time Home Buyers' Property Transfer Tax (PTT) threshold in 2026?

Qualifying first-time buyers in BC receive a full Property Transfer Tax exemption on the first $500,000 of a principal residence with a fair market value up to $835,000 (saving up to $8,000), and a partial sliding-scale exemption between $835,000 and $860,000. See our
First-Time Home Buyer Program BC Guide
for eligibility rules.
How much PTT does a first-time buyer pay on a $750,000 home in BC?

On a $750,000 resale home, regular BC Property Transfer Tax is $13,000 (1% on the first $200,000 plus 2% on the remaining $550,000). With the first-time buyer exemption covering the first $500,000 ($8,000 saved), a qualifying first-time buyer pays $5,000.
How does the Newly Built Home PTT Exemption differ from the First-Time Buyer Exemption?

The BC Newly Built Home Exemption applies to qualifying brand-new homes or presale condos priced up to $1,100,000 (with a partial exemption between $1,100,000 and $1,150,000) for any buyer moving in as their principal residence, even if you have owned a home before.
Can first-time buyers combine the First Home Savings Account (FHSA) and Home Buyers' Plan (HBP)?

Yes. Qualifying first-time buyers can combine tax-free FHSA withdrawals (up to $8,000 per year in contribution room, $40,000 lifetime limit plus investment growth) with up to $60,000 per person from an RRSP under the federal Home Buyers' Plan toward the same home purchase.
How does the First-Time Buyer GST Rebate work on new homes in BC?

Under the federal first-time buyer GST rebate rules for qualifying new construction, eligible first-time buyers can save up to $50,000 (100% of the 5% GST on new homes up to $1,000,000, phasing out between $1,000,000 and $1,500,000). Read our full
First-Time Buyer GST Rebate BC Guide
What happens if only one spouse on title is a first-time home buyer?

If two buyers purchase together and only one qualifies as a first-time buyer, the BC Property Transfer Tax exemption is prorated by the qualifying buyer's registered percentage ownership on title (for example, 50% of the exemption on a 50/50 ownership split).
What occupancy rules must I meet to keep my BC first-time buyer PTT exemption?

For an existing resale home, you must move in within 92 days of the registration date and occupy the property as your principal residence for the remainder of the first full year, or a prorated portion of the tax exemption will be clawed back.
